ApiError.description: The body of every error response.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable identifier such as `unauthorized`.

Cue.description:
One text segment with the time range during which it is shown.

The text keeps any inline markup from the source file, such as `<i>`, and joins
multiple lines with `\n`.

DictionaryLanguages.description: The languages a dictionary translates between, as ISO 639 codes. `null` clears one.

DictionaryLookupResult.description: The entries one dictionary has for a term.

source_language.description: The language of the headwords, as an ISO 639 code, when known.

target_language.description: The language of the definitions, as an ISO 639 code, when known.

EmbeddedSubtitleTrack.description: A subtitle track stored inside a media container.

codec.description: The container's own name for the codec, such as `S_TEXT/UTF8` in Matroska.

language.description: The language tag stored in the container, when there is one.

track_id.description: The container's own id for the track.

oneOf.description: The span of the media file the context audio is cut from.
The media file the card was made from, when it was made from one.

screenshot_ms.description: The media time the screenshot is taken at.

FlashcardDraftRequest.description: Everything the app knows about a word at the moment the user asks for a flashcard.

lemma.description: The dictionary headword, when a lookup found one.

word.description: The word as it appeared in the text.

FlashcardFieldKind.description: The kinds of field a flashcard can have. Each kind appears at most once on a card.

tag_with_media_name.description: Adds a tag made from the media file's name to every new card.

use_tts_when_no_audio.description: Fills the audio fields with synthesized speech when the media has no audio track.

results.description: One result per dictionary that has the term, in import order.

duration_ms.description: Filled in once the file has been opened and its length is known.

name.description: The file name, shown in lists and used as a default flashcard tag.

MediaSource.description:
Where the bytes of a media or subtitle file live.

`path` names a file on the machine running the server, which only the native app can
use. `browser_file` names a file the web app stored in the browser; the server keeps the
key but never resolves it.

NewFlashcard.description: A flashcard as sent to be created or updated: everything but the id and the timestamp.

NewMediaFile.description: The request body for adding a media file to a project.

NewSubtitleTrack.description: The request body for attaching a subtitle track to a media file.

ParseTimedTextRequest.description: The request body shared by the HTTP route and the WebAssembly facade.

PreferenceValue.description: A preference value. `null` means the preference has not been set.

Project.description:
A complete project as the project screen shows it. Flashcards are listed separately,
since a project can hold thousands of them.

last_opened_at.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp. Equals `created_at` until the project is first opened.

ProjectSettings.description:
Everything the new-project form collects. The same type creates a project and updates
its settings later.

target_language.description: The language being learned, as a BCP 47 tag such as `de` or `pt-BR`.

translation_language.description: The language definitions and translations are shown in, as a BCP 47 tag.

ProjectSummary.description: A project as listed on the home screen.

SubtitleTrackSource.description:
Where a subtitle track comes from: a separate file, or a track embedded in the media
container, identified by the container's own track id.

TextSource.description:
Where the text of a request comes from.

The `path` variant names a file on the machine running the server. The server resolves
it, and only for requests authenticated with the per-launch token. The WebAssembly build
supports only the `inline` variant.

TimeRange.description: A span of media time in milliseconds, with `end_ms` exclusive.
